samples.summary: The new `setCursorForHistory` presence write in `insertLink`'s caret branch is exercised by no test at all
samples.evidence: editor.ts:3653-3659 adds a guarded `setCursorForHistory(cursor.position, null)` whose comment claims it fixes a pre-existing undo-caret gap and asserts subtle ordering ("It stays *outside* the batch, unlike the snapshot"). Every docs-package test drives the editor with `MemDocStore` (edit-link-in-place.test.ts:90, table-link.test.ts, link-snap-*.test.ts), and `MemDocStore` has no `setCursorForHistory`, so the `'setCursorForHistory' in docStore` guard is false and the whole block is skipped. On the frontend, the only YorkieDocStore-backed editor undo test is editor-undo-selection.test.ts, which covers `applyStyle`/paste/named styles and never calls `insertLink` (grep for insertLink in packages/frontend/tests matches only slides toolbar tests and the new popover test). So both the presence write and its inside/outside-batch ordering could be wrong or dead and the suite stays green.

samples.summary: Text-box in-place link edit: the new caret move and the inside-the-batch snapshot have no assertions
samples.evidence: text-box-editor.ts now calls `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace(...)` and moves the caret to the returned offset ("Not optional: the caret can otherwise sit past the end of a run the replacement shortened"). packages/docs/test/view/text-box-edit-link-in-place.test.ts only inspects `commitBlocks()[0].inlines` (lines 110-139) — it never reads the caret and never undoes, so the docs-side equivalents ('leaves the caret at the end of the rewritten text', 'an in-place link edit costs exactly one undo step') have no text-box counterpart. A wrong caret offset here (or a double undo step from the snapshot placement) would ship undetected.
searchedFor: grep for caret/cursor assertions in text-box tests
grep undo in text-box test files

samples.summary: No test for the new selection-covers-a-link in-place branch when the selection lives inside a table cell
samples.evidence: The new `linkRunCoveringRange` branch (editor.ts:3607-3630) marks dirty via `dirtyBlockIdsForRange` only, unlike the caret branch below it which maps a cell block to its parent table block. table-link.test.ts's two added tests (#1038) both use a collapsed caret (`restoreLocalCursor` then `insertLink`); no test selects a self-labelled link inside a cell and edits its href, which is exactly the state a drag inside a cell now produces via `setSnappedRange`. A stale/incorrectly-marked table render would not be caught.

samples.summary: The deliberate "shift+arrow does not snap to links" decision is pinned by a comment only, with no test
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:3209-3218 documents at length that keyboard shift+arrow must NOT run the link snap, in contrast to every pointer gesture. No test asserts it: grep for shiftKey in packages/docs/test finds no keyboard test extending a selection one character into a link, and link-snap-pointer.test.ts / link-snap-header-drag.test.ts only dispatch mouse events. A future refactor that routes the keyboard branch through `setSnappedRange` would silently make single-character selection into a link impossible.

samples.summary: Triple-click paragraph select and the in-cell gestures were rerouted through `setSnappedRange` with no coverage for either
samples.evidence: The triple-click body path (text-editor.ts:2052-2058) is routed through `setSnappedRange` specifically "so a shift+click afterwards extends from the paragraph start", and the in-cell branches (lines ~1987-2038) were changed the same way, including `rawAnchor` assignment on single click in a cell. link-snap-pointer.test.ts covers double-click + shift+click in the body only (its `doubleClick` helper never triple-clicks), and no test performs any pointer gesture over a hyperlink inside a table cell. Both claimed behaviours could regress unnoticed.
searchedFor: grep rawAnchor across packages (only selection-raw-anchor + link-snap tests)

samples.summary: Popover Apply-guard tests cover only the `editRequest` entry point and a caret-shaped editor stub; the view-mode Edit path and the drag-selection case are untested
samples.evidence: All six tests call `renderPopover(editor, initialUrl)`, which always supplies `editRequest`, so the `handleEdit` branch (docs-link-popover.tsx:139-141) that also sets `editingHref` from `linkInfo.href` is never entered — the guard could be missing there and every test still passes. The stub's `getLinkAtCursor` is a plain closure, so nothing checks the guard against the real editor semantics for a *range* selection (with a drag-snapped link, `getLinkAtCursor` answers from the focus position at the link's boundary); if that answered `undefined`, Apply would refuse every drag-then-⌘K edit and no test in either package would notice.

samples.summary: Test comments cite a press offset the test never performs ("raw press at 8" vs `press(12)`)
samples.evidence: link-snap-pointer.test.ts:211 presses at offset 12, but the comments at lines 221-222 and 235-236 both reason about "the raw press at 8". Both offsets are mid-link so the assertions still hold, but the mismatch makes it hard to tell whether the test exercises the scenario it documents.

samples.summary: Header-drag test's global prototype patches are never restored
samples.evidence: `installCanvasShim()` overwrites `HTMLCanvasElement.prototype.getContext`, `globalThis.ResizeObserver` and `HTMLElement.prototype.getBoundingClientRect` (lines 25-63) with no saved originals; `afterEach` (lines 154-158) restores only `requestAnimationFrame`. link-snap-pointer.test.ts by contrast saves and restores each. Harmless under per-file isolation, but it makes the fixture unsafe to reuse and can mask geometry failures if isolation is ever relaxed.

verdict.reason: The guarded presence write at editor.ts:3653-3659 can only execute when the injected store implements setCursorForHistory, and the sole implementation is YorkieDocStore (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3048). Every docs-package test that drives insertLink uses MemDocStore (memory.ts:32, which has no such method) - edit-link-in-place.test.ts:90, link-snap-header-drag.test.ts:92, hf-cursor-screen-rect.test.ts:257, editor-read-only.test.ts:315 - so the guard is false and the block is skipped. The only test-only store subclass that adds optional presence hooks (caret-line-affinity.test.ts:80 PresenceMemDocStore) implements only getPresenceCursorPos/getPresenceSelection. The only YorkieDocStore-backed editor-API test, editor-undo-selection.test.ts (read in full), exercises applyStyle/paste/named styles and never calls insertLink; all frontend insertLink references are vi.fn() mocks (docs-link-popover.test.tsx:25, docs-context-menu.test.tsx:18). yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:364-512 covers setCursorForHistory only at the store level, not through the link path. No e2e suite exists (glob for **/e2e/** returned nothing). Hence both the presence write and its asserted outside-the-batch ordering are untested: a broken or dead write leaves the suite green while undo silently fails to restore the caret after an in-place href edit, a user-visible path.
